events.text: Objective: Determine whether there is sufficient public evidence to justify Aquaporin A/S investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current water-membrane offering.. Constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.; Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.; Evidence must demonstrate demand, willingness to pay, or a viable route to market for a differentiated consumer proposition.; Any recommendation must be based on observable data, not assumptions.. Alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting a specific use case (e.g., home water purifier for a niche segment).; 2) Expand the existing water‑membrane offering to new markets or customer segments without a differentiated proposition (e.g., B2B expansion).; 3) No expansion: continue focusing on current B2B membranes and existing distribution channels.; 4) Change the route to market (e.g., direct‑to‑consumer e‑commerce, partnerships with retailers) without altering the product proposition..

T1: Consumers will adopt a differentiated home water purifier if they perceive it as a premium, health‑focused product that offers superior taste and purity, leading them to pay a premium price. Who benefits: Health‑conscious consumers seeking higher purity and better taste in drinking water.. Why behaviour changes: If consumers shift from viewing water purifiers as a necessity to a lifestyle or health product, they will be willing to purchase a premium‑priced purifier that justifies the cost.. How value is captured: Aquaporin can capture value by pricing the differentiated product at a premium, selling through direct‑to‑consumer channels or premium retailers, and leveraging brand positioning as a premium water‑purification solution.. Assumptions: Consumers are willing to pay more for perceived health and taste benefits.; The premium positioning can be effectively communicated to the target segment.; Distribution channels can reach the premium segment without significant cost.. Predictions: In a test offering a premium‑priced differentiated purifier, purchase intent or actual sales will be higher than for a standard‑priced model.; Surveyed consumers will rank taste and purity as top reasons for purchasing the premium product..

T2: Consumers will adopt a differentiated home water purifier if it is marketed as a sustainable, eco‑friendly product that reduces plastic waste, leading them to choose it over conventional purifiers. Who benefits: Environmentally conscious consumers who prioritize reducing single‑use plastic consumption.. Why behaviour changes: If consumers associate water purifiers with sustainability and waste reduction, they will be motivated to switch from existing products, even if the cost is higher.. How value is captured: Aquaporin can capture value by positioning the product as a sustainable solution, pricing it at a premium for eco‑conscious buyers, and selling through channels that emphasize environmental messaging.. Assumptions: Consumers are willing to pay more for a product that reduces plastic waste.; Environmental messaging can effectively influence purchase decisions.; Distribution channels can highlight sustainability attributes without compromising margins.. Predictions: In a test offering a sustainability‑focused differentiated purifier, purchase intent or actual sales will be higher than for a standard‑priced model.; Surveyed consumers will rank sustainability as a top reason for purchasing the product..

Test "Premium vs Sustainability Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging condition. Participants view a product description of a differentiated home water purifier (e.g., premium taste and purity) and a description emphasizing sustainability and plastic waste reduction. They are then asked to indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1‑2 "Very unlikely" to 7 "Very likely").. Sample: 300 adult consumers in Denmark, recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and income. Randomly assigned to one of two conditions: Premium Condition (premium taste and purity messaging) or Sustainability Condition (sustainability and plastic waste reduction messaging).. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑2 to 7) for each condition.. Predictions: T1: Premium Condition will yield a mean purchase intent score ≥ 5.5, significantly higher than Sustainability Condition.; T2: Sustainability Condition will yield a mean purchase intent score ≥ 5.5, significantly higher than Premium Condition.. Decision rule: If Premium Condition mean ≥ 5.5 and Sustainability Condition mean < 5.5, recommend developing a differentiated consumer proposition focused on premium taste and purity. If Sustainability Condition mean ≥ 5.5 and Premium Condition mean < 5.5, recommend a sustainability‑focused proposition. If both conditions meet their respective thresholds, conduct a. Cost: 18000 euros, 10 weeks.

Favours T1: Do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition yet. Public evidence does not demonstrate consumer demand for premium taste and purity, nor does it address sustainability motivations. Conduct a small-scale test (e.g., the proposed Premium vs Sustainability Messaging Test) before committing resources. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Recommendation: Do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition yet. Public evidence does not demonstrate consumer demand for premium taste and purity, nor does it address sustainability motivations. Conduct a small-scale test (e.g., the proposed Premium vs Sustainability Messaging Test) before committing resources. Target customer: Health‑conscious consumers who prioritize higher purity and better taste in drinking water.. Value proposition: A differentiated home water purifier positioned as a premium, easy‑to‑use solution that delivers superior taste and purity, justified by a premium price point.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the Premium vs Sustainability Messaging Test (300 Danish adults, 10‑week timeline, €18,000 budget) to measure purchase intent under each messaging condition.. Uncertainty: The size of the premium‑priced consumer market and the willingness to pay for taste and purity are unknown. Sustainability demand remains uncertain and could be driven by other factors.. Would change if: If the Premium Condition mean purchase intent score falls below 5.5, indicating insufficient demand for premium positioning.; If the Sustainability Condition mean purchase intent score falls below 5.5, indicating insufficient demand for eco‑friendly positioning.; If new evidence shows strong consumer demand for either premium taste or sustainability attributes, the recommendation would shift accordingly.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

events.text: Objective: Determine whether there is sufficient public evidence to justify Electron’x Professional Group investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current professional laundry offering.. Constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.; Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.; Must identify evidence of consumer demand, willingness to pay, and competitive positioning.; Must consider existing consumer reach (if any) and the feasibility of reaching it.; Any recommendation must be based on observable demand, not assumptions.. Alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting a specific use case (e.g., home laundry, small businesses, or a new segment).; 2) Expand the existing professional offering into adjacent consumer segments without a differentiated proposition (e.g., add consumer‑focused features to professional models).; 3) No expansion: continue focusing exclusively on professional laundry and food‑service equipment.; 4) Change the route to market for existing professional products to reach consumers directly (e.g., online sales, retail partnerships).; 5) Target a different customer group within the professional segment (e.g., small hotels, gyms, or healthcare facilities) with a differentiated proposition..

T1: Home consumers increasingly adopt self-service laundry for convenience and cost savings, creating demand for compact, reliable consumer-grade machines that fit small spaces. Who benefits: Individual renters, small businesses, and apartment-dwelling households seeking affordable, easy-to-use laundry solutions.. Why behaviour changes: Growing awareness of energy efficiency and lower utility costs make home self-service machines attractive compared to traditional laundromats.. How value is captured: Electrolux can sell compact, premium-priced machines directly to consumers through retail and wholesale channels, earning higher margins than bulk professional sales.. Assumptions: Consumer self-service demand is growing in residential markets.; Consumers are willing to pay a premium for compact, professional-grade machines.; Electrolux's existing professional technology can be adapted to a consumer format without major redesign.. Predictions: A targeted consumer survey would show >30% of respondents considering a home self-service machine within 12 months.; Sales of compact professional machines would increase in regions with high urban density and low laundromat availability.; Price sensitivity tests would reveal consumers willing to pay 15-20% above standard professional machines for space-saving features..

T2: Small businesses and hospitality operators increasingly adopt self-service laundry to reduce labor costs and improve operational efficiency, creating demand for compact, reliable machines that fit limited spaces. Who benefits: Small hotels, gyms, marina staff, and other small businesses with limited laundry space.. Why behaviour changes: Labor shortages and rising wage costs make automated self-service solutions financially attractive, and the need to serve guests or members quickly drives adoption.. How value is captured: Electrolux can sell compact professional machines through wholesale and retail channels, offering volume discounts and service contracts that lock in recurring revenue.. Assumptions: Small business labor costs are rising in key markets.; Self-service adoption is driven by operational efficiency, not just convenience.; Electrolux's professional machines can be adapted to small business needs without major redesign.. Predictions: A survey of small hospitality operators would show >40% considering self-service machines within 12 months.; Sales of compact professional machines would increase in regions with high small business density.; Price sensitivity tests would reveal small businesses willing to pay 10-15% above standard professional machines for space-saving features..

Test "Segmented Messaging Test for Consumer and Small Business Messaging" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging exposure. Participants are randomly assigned to one of three message frames: (1) home self-service convenience (space-saving, lower utility costs); (2) small business labor cost savings (automated, quick turnout); (3) neutral control. After viewing the message, participants indicate likelihood to purchase a compact professional machine at a premium price (15-20% above standard professional machines).. Sample: 500 respondents: 200 in the United States, 200 in a region with high small business density (e.g., California), and 100 in a region with high urban density and few laundromats.. Measure: Purchase intent rate (percentage of respondents indicating "very likely" to purchase) for each message frame.. Predictions: T1: Home self-service frame will generate the highest purchase intent (>=35%) among U.S. respondents.; T2: Small business frame will generate the highest purchase intent (>=35%) among California respondents.. Decision rule: If the purchase intent for the home self-service frame exceeds 35% in the U.S. and the small business frame does not, proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting home renters. If the small business frame exceeds 35% in California and the home frame does not, develop a small business proposition. If neither frame reaches 35%, do not expand into consumer segments.. Cost: 18000 euros, 8 weeks.

Favours T1: Conduct the proposed segmented messaging test (X1) to empirically compare consumer and small business demand. If the home self-service frame achieves >=35% purchase intent in the U.S., develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting home renters. If the small business frame achieves >=35% intent in California, develop a small business proposition. If neither frame reaches 35%, do not expand into consumer or B Beliefs: T1: uncertain; T2: uncertain.

New claim: Home consumers increasingly adopt self-service laundry for convenience and cost savings, creating demand for compact, reliable consumer-grade machines that fit small spaces.. Evidence: SYN-D.

Recommendation: Run the proposed segmented messaging test (X1) to empirically compare consumer and small business demand. If the home self-service frame achieves >=35% purchase intent in the U.S., develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting home renters. If the small business frame achieves >=35% intent in California, develop a small business proposition. If neither frame reaches 35%, do not expand into consumer segments Target customer: Home renters and small businesses (hotels, gyms, marinas) with limited laundry space.. Value proposition: Compact, professional-grade self-service machines that offer space savings, lower utility costs, and reliable performance for residential and small business users.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Execute the 8‑week, €18,000 online survey with randomized messaging exposure, analyzing purchase intent by segment.. Uncertainty: Both T1 and T2 remain uncertain due to lack of direct evidence on consumer willingness to pay and small business demand. The test will resolve this.. Would change if: If the home self-service frame fails to achieve >=35% purchase intent in the U.S., the recommendation would shift to focus on small business demand.; If the small business frame fails to achieve >=35% intent in California, the recommendation would shift to focus on small business demand.; If neither frame reaches 35%, the recommendation would be to avoid expansion into consumer segments.. Beliefs: T1: uncertain; T2: uncertain.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 household washing-machine buyers eligible for the same professional-derived washer offer were assigned equally to two descriptions. Both descriptions showed the same machine, brand, price, warranty, availability, service terms and verified specifications. One emphasized durability and repairability; the other emphasized washing performance and the upfront price. No discount or extra service was added. The outcome was a paid, refundable purchase reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned buyers per arm. There were 32 reservations in the durability-and-repairability description arm and 72 in the performance-and-price description arm. This tests the incremental effect of the description in this recruited population, not actual appliance lifetime, delivery capability, market size, profitability or sustained repurchase. A weaker result would not refute a different channel or product theory.

sources.excerpt: On February 6, 2017, Anova was acquired by Electrolux , a home appliance company, for a total of US$250 million.

Subsequent products included the Anova Precision Cooker Nano and the Anova Precision Oven, a countertop combi oven that supported both steam and convection cooking methods and could be used either alongside other Precision Cooker products or by itself.
These countertop appliances have the same characteristic changes as the full-size household appliances, except that they are smaller, and cost significantly less than a full-size oven.
Many models have a water container that can be filled from the front, eliminating the need for a water line connection. Some units can run on only single-phase or split-phase electric current.
Germany: RATIONAL AG , Gaggenau Hausgeräte , PALUX, Convotherm, MKN, ELOMA, Miele , AEG (part of Electrolux), Bosch.

The customer base ranges from restaurants and hotels, company canteens, hospitals, schools, universities, the military, prisons and retirement homes to fast-food restaurants, party services, supermarkets, bakeries and snack bars, butchers, petrol stations and delivery services, including so-called ghost kitchens.
key figures from 2024: 50% global market share, sales of EUR 1,194 million, EBIT of EUR 314 million, EBIT margin of 26%, equity ratio of 77%, dividend payout ratio of 68%.
RATIONAL AG is the global market and technology leader for innovative cooking systems in commercial food preparation.
According to company estimates, the global market potential for combi-steamers is 4.8 million customers, around 75% of whom still use traditional cooking appliances.
the Rational Group’s sales revenues reached a new record of 1.194 billion euros in 2024 (2023: 1.126 billion euros), an increase of 68 million euros or 6 percent compared to the previous year.
From 1978 onwards, the company concentrated solely on combi steamers and discontinued all other product lines.

T1: Home cooks will adopt a differentiated combi-steamer if it is marketed as a smart, subscription-based device that learns cooking preferences and delivers recipes, because they value convenience and personalized cooking. Who benefits: Home cooks seeking time-saving, recipe-driven cooking.. Why behaviour changes: Smart features and subscription services reduce the learning curve and provide ongoing content, making the appliance feel indispensable.. How value is captured: RATIONAL can charge a monthly subscription for recipe updates, smart features, and support, generating recurring revenue while leveraging its existing combi-steamer technology.. Assumptions: Home cooks are willing to pay for smart and subscription services.; Smart features are perceived as a significant advantage over traditional ovens.; Subscription model can be scaled without eroding brand loyalty.. Predictions: Surveyed home cooks will indicate willingness to pay a monthly subscription fee for smart features.; Pilot participants will show higher repeat purchase rates for subscription-enabled devices compared to non-subscription-enabled devices.; Sales of subscription-enabled models will exceed sales of non-subscription-enabled models in the same segment..

T2: Home cooks will adopt a differentiated combi-steamer if it is positioned as a premium, design‑focused appliance that signals status and quality, because they view cooking as a lifestyle and are willing to pay for brand prestige. Who benefits: Affluent home cooks who use cooking as a status symbol and are willing to invest in high‑end appliances.. Why behaviour changes: Design, brand prestige, and the perception of quality create a willingness to pay a premium price for a product that is seen as a status item.. How value is captured: RATIONAL can command higher price points, sell through premium retail channels, and capture value through limited‑edition designs and brand storytelling.. Assumptions: Design and brand prestige are primary purchase drivers for home cooks.; Affluent consumers are willing to pay a premium for a product that signals status.; Premium positioning can be sustained without eroding market share in the mass market.. Predictions: Surveyed home cooks will rank design and brand prestige higher than functionality when choosing a combi-steamer.; Premium‑priced models will show higher average transaction value than standard‑priced models.; Limited‑edition or design‑focused models will generate higher repeat purchase rates among premium‑priced buyers..

T3: Home cooks will adopt a differentiated combi-steamer if it is marketed as a health‑focused, low‑impact cooking solution that emphasizes steam‑based, nutrient‑retaining meals, because they seek healthier alternatives to traditional cooking. Who benefits: Health‑conscious home cooks who prioritize nutrient retention and low‑impact cooking.. Why behaviour changes: Health messaging and the perception of steam‑based cooking as a healthier option create a willingness to switch from traditional ovens.. How value is captured: RATIONAL can position the appliance as a health‑focused product, command higher price points, and sell through health‑focused retail channels, capturing value through premium positioning and brand association with wellness.. Assumptions: Health‑conscious consumers are willing to pay a premium for a product marketed as low‑impact.; Steam‑based cooking is perceived as a healthier cooking method compared to traditional methods.; Health messaging can be sustained without eroding market share in the mass market.. Predictions: Surveyed home cooks will rank health and low‑impact attributes higher than functionality when choosing a combi‑steamer.; Health‑focused models will show higher average transaction value than standard‑priced models.; Marketing health messaging will increase purchase intent among health‑conscious consumers..

Test "Smart vs Premium vs Health Messaging Test" between T1; T2; T3. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging exposure. Participants are randomly assigned to one of three groups: Smart Group (smart features and subscription messaging), Premium Group (design and brand prestige messaging), Health Group (health and low-impact messaging). Each group sees a product description of a differentiated combi-steamer and is asked to indicate willingness to pay a fixed price (e.g., €1,200) and to choose a purchase channel (online, retail).. Sample: 300 adult home cooks recruited via an online panel, balanced across the three groups (100 per group).. Measure: 1) Willingness to pay (WTP) in euros. 2) Purchase intent (binary: would buy). 3) Channel preference (online vs retail).. Predictions: T1: Smart Group will show the highest WTP and purchase intent among home cooks, while Premium and Health Groups will show lower WTP and purchase intent.; T2: Premium Group will show the highest WTP and purchase intent, while Smart and Health Groups will show lower WTP and purchase intent.; T3: Health Group will show the highest WTP and purchase intent, while Smart and Premium Groups will show lower WTP and purchase intent.. Decision rule: If the Smart Group's average WTP is at least 20% higher than the Premium Group's and at least 15% higher than the Health Group's, we conclude that smart features drive adoption and recommend developing a differentiated home-cook proposition with smart and subscription capabilities. If the Premium Group's average WTP is at least 20% higher than the Smart Group's and at least 15% higher than the Health Group's, we conclude that design and brand prestige drive adoption and recommend a premium positioning. If the Health Group's average WTP is at least 20% higher than the Smart Group's and at least 15% higher than the Premium Group's, we conclude that health messaging drives adoption and recommend a health-focused proposition. If none of these thresholds are met, we conclude insufficient evidence to favor any theory and recommend no expansion.. Cost: 20000 euros, 6 weeks.

Favours T1: Develop a differentiated home-cook proposition that integrates smart features and a subscription model, leveraging RATIONAL’s existing combi-steamer technology to address home cooks’ demand for convenience and personalized cooking. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain; T3: uncertain.

Recommendation: Develop a differentiated home-cook proposition that integrates smart features and a subscription model, leveraging RATIONAL’s existing combi-steamer technology to address home cooks’ demand for convenience and personalized cooking. Target customer: Affluent, tech‑savvy home cooks who value convenience, personalized cooking, and are willing to pay for smart and subscription services.. Value proposition: A smart, subscription‑enabled combi‑steamer that learns cooking preferences, delivers recipes, and provides ongoing support, offering a convenient, personalized cooking experience at a premium price point.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Smart vs Premium vs Health Messaging Test (300 participants, 6‑week timeline, €20,000 budget) to measure willingness to pay, purchase intent, and channel preference across the three messaging groups.. Uncertainty: The test will determine whether smart features, design and brand prestige, or health messaging drive adoption. Current evidence is limited to company assertions and market facts, and no direct consumer survey data is available.. Would change if: If the Smart Group shows a willingness to pay at least 20% higher than the Premium Group and at least 15% higher than the Health Group, we would shift focus to smart‑feature positioning.; If the Premium Group shows a willingness to pay at least 20% higher than the Smart Group and at least 15% higher than the Health Group, we would shift focus to premium positioning.; If the Health Group shows a willingness to pay at least 20% higher than the Smart Group and at least 15% higher than the Premium Group, we would shift focus to health‑focused positioning.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain; T3: uncertain.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 household washing-machine buyers eligible for the same professional-derived washer offer were assigned equally to two descriptions. Both descriptions showed the same machine, brand, price, warranty, availability, service terms and verified specifications. One emphasized durability and repairability; the other emphasized washing performance and the upfront price. No discount or extra service was added. The outcome was a paid, refundable purchase reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned buyers per arm. There were 32 reservations in the durability-and-repairability description arm and 72 in the performance-and-price description arm. This tests the incremental effect of the description in this recruited population, not actual appliance lifetime, delivery capability, market size, profitability or sustained repurchase. A weaker result would not refute a different channel or product theory.

Test "Consumer vs Professional Intent Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized exposure to either a consumer‑grade self‑service machine description (focusing on convenience, space‑saving, and self‑operation) or a professional‑grade high‑cycle machine description (focusing on durability, reliability, and staff‑operation). Participants are recruited from homeowners (n . Sample: 300 participants: 150 homeowners (renters and first‑time buyers) and 150 small‑business professionals (gyms, marinas, campsites). Randomly assigned to either exposure group.. Measure: Purchase intent measured on a 7‑point Likert scale (1‑not likely, 7‑very likely) and binary intent to purchase within 12 weeks.. Predictions: T1: Homeowners exposed to consumer‑grade description will show higher average intent than professionals exposed to professional‑grade description, and both groups will be above 5 on the intent scale.; T2: Professionals exposed to professional‑grade description will show higher average intent than homeowners exposed to consumer‑grade description, and both groups will be above 5 on the intent scale.. Decision rule: If the average intent for the exposed group is at least 5.5 points higher than the other group, proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition for that segment. If the difference is less than 1.5 points, do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition. If the difference is less than 0.5 points, conduct a larger pilot test before committing.. Cost: 18000 euros, 10 weeks.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited home cooks considering the same professional-derived combi-steamer were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed identical equipment, brand, cooking specifications, total installed price, warranty, available delivery dates and eventual plumbing/electrical work. One offer bundled an installation coordinator and a site-readiness checklist; the other required the purchaser to arrange the same qualified installers directly. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. All recruited homes were eligible for the stated installation work. The outcome was a paid refundable reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days among all 400 assigned households per arm. There were 72 reservations for the coordinated-installation offer and 32 for the purchaser-arranged offer. This tests whether coordination friction changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show that the appliance fits ordinary kitchens, eliminates drain or power requirements, earns a margin, or justifies diverting resources from professional customers. It does not establish market size or a need for new RATIONAL hardware. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow coordination mechanism changes.

T1: Consumers will adopt a differentiated home water purifier if they perceive it as a premium, health‑focused product that offers superior taste and purity, leading them to pay a premium price. Who benefits: Health‑conscious consumers seeking higher purity and better taste in drinking water.. Why behaviour changes: If consumers shift from viewing water purifiers as a necessity to a lifestyle or health product, they will be willing to purchase a premium‑priced purifier that justifies the cost.. How value is captured: Aquaporin can capture value by pricing the differentiated product at a premium, selling through direct‑to‑consumer channels or premium retailers, and leveraging brand positioning as a premium water‑purification solution.. Assumptions: Consumers are willing to pay more for perceived health and taste benefits.; The premium positioning can be effectively communicated to the target segment.; Distribution channels can reach the premium segment without significant cost.. Predictions: In a test offering a premium‑priced differentiated purifier, purchase intent or actual sales will be higher than for a standard‑priced model.; Surveyed consumers will rank taste and purity as top reasons for purchasing the premium product..

T2: Consumers will adopt a differentiated home water purifier if it is marketed as a sustainable, eco‑friendly product that reduces plastic waste, leading them to choose it over conventional purifiers. Who benefits: Environmentally conscious consumers who prioritize reducing single‑use plastic consumption.. Why behaviour changes: If consumers associate water purifiers with sustainability and waste reduction, they will be motivated to switch from existing products, even if the cost is higher.. How value is captured: Aquaporin can capture value by positioning the product as a sustainable solution, pricing it at a premium for eco‑conscious buyers, and selling through channels that emphasize environmental messaging.. Assumptions: Consumers are willing to pay more for a product that reduces plastic waste.; Environmental messaging can effectively influence purchase decisions.; Distribution channels can highlight sustainability attributes without compromising margins.. Predictions: In a test offering a sustainability‑focused differentiated purifier, purchase intent or actual sales will be higher than for a standard‑priced model.; Surveyed consumers will rank sustainability as a top reason for purchasing the product..

Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: Group A sees a premium‑priced purifier messaging emphasizing taste and purity; Group B sees a sustainability‑focused purifier messaging emphasizing reduced plastic waste. Participants indicate purchase intent on a 7‑point scale (1‑not at all likely to 7‑extremely likely) and state their top reason for choosing the product.. Sample: 400 adult consumers in Denmark, recruited via an online panel, balanced across both groups (200 per group).. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑to 7) and top reason for choosing the product.. Predictions: T1: Group A will have a higher average purchase intent score than Group B, and taste and purity will be the top reason for Group A.; T2: Group B will have a higher average purchase intent score than Group A, and sustainability will be the top reason for Group B.. If neither difference meets the threshold, do not invest in a differentiated proposition and continue focusing on current B2B membranes.. Cost: 18000 euros, 6 weeks.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 households already using a compatible drinking-water purifier received the same membrane specifications, water-quality information, brand, warranty and total annual price. Half were offered a prepaid plan with scheduled cartridge delivery and replacement reminders; half were offered a prepaid self-service cartridge plan without that delivery schedule or reminders. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid plan enrollment remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned households per arm. This what-if assumes an authorised operator can legally supply and service the offer; it does not change the dossier evidence about Aquaporin's insolvency or financing. There were 120 plan enrollments in the scheduled-delivery-and-reminder plan arm and 60 in the self-service cartridge plan arm. This tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under that conditional supply assumption, not membrane efficacy, correct long-term filter use, market size, company solvency or Aquaporin's ability to fund an offer. An unchanged business recommendation can be justified by those other constraints.

Test "Premium vs Sustainability Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging condition. Participants view a product description of a differentiated home water purifier (e.g., premium health benefits and taste) and a description emphasizing sustainability and plastic waste reduction. They are then asked to indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1‑10) and to state the top reason for choosing the product.. Sample: 300 adult consumers in Denmark, recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and income to ensure representativeness.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) and top reason for choosing the product.. Predictions: T1: Participants exposed to premium messaging will report higher purchase intent and will cite taste and purity as the top reason.; T2: Participants exposed to sustainability messaging will report higher purchase intent and will cite sustainability as the top reason.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent score for premium messaging is at least 5 points higher than for sustainability messaging (i.e., premium ≥ 5.5 and sustainability ≤ 5.0), proceed with a premium‑priced differentiated proposition. If the difference is less than 2 points, consider a sustainability‑focused proposition. If the difference is ≤ 2 points, do not commit to either proposition and conduct further market research.. Cost: 2000 euros, 4 weeks.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 home espresso enthusiasts considering the same Simonelli single-group machine were assigned equally to two offers. Machine, brand, price, warranty, availability and total contact time were identical. One offer included a structured hands-on home-barista setup lesson; the other included an equal-length product-specification orientation without a skill lesson. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid, refundable machine reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned enthusiasts per arm. There were 32 reservations in the home-barista-lesson offer arm and 72 in the product-specification-orientation offer arm. This tests the incremental effect of this learning offer among recruited enthusiasts, not a need for a new machine, demand among ordinary coffee drinkers, commercial margins or lasting skill retention. It does not show that every hobby or status mechanism is true or false.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited home cooks considering the same professional-derived combi-steamer were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed identical equipment, brand, cooking specifications, total installed price, warranty, available delivery dates and eventual plumbing/electrical work. One offer bundled an installation coordinator and a site-readiness checklist; the other required the purchaser to arrange the same qualified installers directly. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. All recruited homes were eligible for the stated installation work. The outcome was a paid refundable reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days among all 400 assigned households per arm. There were 32 reservations for the coordinated-installation offer and 72 for the purchaser-arranged offer. This tests whether coordination friction changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show that the appliance fits ordinary kitchens, eliminates drain or power requirements, earns a margin, or justifies diverting resources from professional customers. It does not establish market size or a need for new RATIONAL hardware. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow coordination mechanism changes.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 home espresso enthusiasts considering the same Simonelli single-group machine were assigned equally to two offers. Machine, brand, price, warranty, availability and total contact time were identical. One offer included a structured hands-on home-barista setup lesson; the other included an equal-length product-specification orientation without a skill lesson. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid, refundable machine reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned enthusiasts per arm. There were 72 reservations in the home-barista-lesson offer arm and 32 in the product-specification-orientation offer arm. This tests the incremental effect of this learning offer among recruited enthusiasts, not a need for a new machine, demand among ordinary coffee drinkers, commercial margins or lasting skill retention. It does not show that every hobby or status mechanism is true or false.

Randomly assign participants to one of two groups: Group A (lifestyle positioning) and Group B (practical positioning). Both groups view a simulated Simonelli consumer product (e.g., compact espresso machine) and are asked: "How much would you pay for this product?" (willingness to pay in euros).. Sample: 300 home barista consumers (self-identified) from Europe, recruited via online panels.. Measure: Average willingness to pay (WTP) in euros for the simulated Simonelli consumer product.. Predictions: T1: Group A will show a WTP at least 20% higher than Group B, indicating willingness to pay a premium for lifestyle positioning.; T2: Group A will show a WTP equal to or lower than Group B, indicating the market is small and unprofitable.. Decision rule: If the average WTP for Group A exceeds Group B by at least 20% (e.g., Group A: €120 vs Group B: €100), proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition. T2: Home barista demand is driven by the desire for convenience and ease of use, particularly for busy professionals who need quick, high-quality coffee without the hassle of manual brewing. Why behaviour changes: Consumers shift to home brewing when they find a machine that simplifies the process, reduces preparation time, and delivers consistent results.. Test "Home Barista Preference Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with a choice-based conjoint design. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two conditions: social positioning condition (emphasizing the third-place coffee experience) or convenience positioning condition (emphasizing quick, easy brewing). They are then shown a product description of a compact, feature-rich espresso machine and asked to indicate their willingness to pay (WTP) and likelihood to purchase on a 7-point scale.. Sample: 300 participants, recruited from a panel of home baristas and coffee enthusiasts, balanced across the two conditions.. Measure: Average willingness to pay (WTP) and purchase intent (on a 7-point scale) for each condition.. Predictions: T1: Higher average WTP and purchase intent in the social positioning condition compared to the convenience condition.; T2: Higher average WTP and purchase intent in the convenience positioning condition compared to the social positioning condition.. Decision rule: If the average WTP in the social positioning condition exceeds the average WTP in the convenience positioning condition by at least 1.5 points on the 7-point scale, we conclude that social interaction drives demand and support T1. If the average WTP in the convenience positioning condition exceeds the average WTP in the social positioning condition by at least 1.5 points, we conclude that convenience drives demand and support T2. If the difference is within 1.5 points or both conditions show similar WTP, we conclude the evidence is inconclusive and the theories remain open.. Cost: 2000 euros, 4 weeks.

T1 kept: The simulated warehouse test (SYN-D) concerns packing errors and does not address consumer motivations such as social interaction or convenience. Therefore it does not affect T1. Recommendation: Simonelli should develop a differentiated consumer proposition that emphasizes the social coffee experience, positioning its machines as premium, third-place coffee experiences. This aligns with the growing demand for social interaction and the willingness to pay for a premium coffee experience. Target customer: Home baristas and coffee enthusiasts who value the social aspect of coffee culture and are willing to invest in a premium machine that offers a third-place coffee experience.. Value proposition: A compact, feature-rich espresso machine that delivers a premium coffee experience, complemented by social positioning, community events, and accessories that enhance the social aspect of coffee.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Conduct the proposed Home Barista Preference Test to empirically validate whether social positioning drives higher willingness to pay and purchase intent compared to convenience positioning.. Uncertainty: The evidence base is limited to public sources, and no internal company data is available. The test budget and timeline are assumptions; actual results may differ. The market for home barista equipment is also subject to broader economic sl. Would change if: If the test shows that convenience positioning yields significantly higher willingness to pay and purchase intent than social positioning, the recommendation would shift to emphasize convenience and develop a differentiated consumer product; If new independent evidence shows strong demand for social interaction or a significant shift in consumer behavior, the recommendation would be revised to reflect those findings. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

events.text: Objective: Determine whether there is sufficient public evidence to justify Electron’x Professional Group investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current professional laundry offering.. Constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.; Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.; Must identify evidence of consumer demand, willingness to pay, and competitive positioning.; Must consider existing consumer reach (if any) and the feasibility of reaching it.; Any recommendation must be based on observable demand, not assumptions.. Alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting a specific use case (e.g., home laundry, small businesses, or a new segment).; 2) Expand the existing professional offering into adjacent consumer segments without a differentiated proposition (e.g., add consumer‑focused features to professional models).; 3) No expansion: continue focusing exclusively on professional laundry and food‑service equipment.; 4) Change the route to market for existing professional products to reach consumers directly (e.g., online sales, retail partnerships).; 5) Target a different customer group within the professional segment (e.g., small hotels, gyms, or healthcare facilities) with a differentiated proposition..

T1: Homeowners and renters will purchase consumer-grade laundry machines at higher price points because they view them as a convenience and status upgrade, not just a functional appliance. Who benefits: Homeowners, renters, and small landlords seeking convenience and modern aesthetics.. Why behaviour changes: Growing consumer demand for stylish, integrated home appliances and the convenience of self-service laundry reduce perceived utility of basic, utility-style appliances.. How value is captured: Electrolux can charge premium prices for design, smart features, and brand positioning, and potentially license its technology to brands for consumer machines.. Assumptions: Consumers perceive self-service laundry as a modern amenity.; Price sensitivity for home buyers is lower than for professional buyers.; Electrolux's design credibility can be leveraged in consumer markets.. Predictions: Willingness-to-pay studies show consumers will pay at least 20% more for a designer self-service unit than a standard machine.; Consumer surveys indicate a desire for aesthetic integration with home decor.; Pilot sales show higher conversion rates for premium-priced units in pilot markets..

T2: Small businesses and rental properties will adopt consumer-grade laundry machines because they need reliable, low-cost solutions for guest laundry and staff facilities, and existing professional machines are too expensive or difficult to service. Who benefits: Small hotels, gyms, campsites, marinas, and rental property owners with limited budgets.. Why behaviour changes: High turnover of guest laundry and staff facilities makes it cheaper to replace machines than to upgrade, and consumers prefer machines that are easy to maintain and repair.. How value is captured: Electrolux can sell lower-priced, easier-to-service units through retail and wholesale channels, and potentially offer service contracts to reduce downtime.. Assumptions: Small businesses have limited capital for new equipment.; Current professional machines are difficult to repair or replace.; Consumers prioritize ease of maintenance over brand prestige.. Predictions: Small business surveys show higher purchase intent for machines priced under $2,000 compared to professional-grade units.; Pilot sales in rental properties show higher adoption rates for machines with modular designs.; Customer satisfaction surveys highlight ease of repair as a key purchase driver..

Test "Premium vs. Value Messaging Pilot" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with simulated purchase scenarios and willingness-to-pay (WTP) questions.. Sample: 500 respondents: 250 homeowners/renters and 250 small business owners/rental property managers, recruited via panel to match demographics.. Measure: Average WTP (in euros) for a self-service laundry unit described with either premium design features (status upgrade) or cost-ease-of-maintain features (small business). Secondary measure: stated purchase intent (1‑10).. Predictions: T1: Homeowners will show higher WTP for premium-priced units (e.g., €1,500‑€2,000) than small businesses will show higher WTP for value-priced units (e.g., €1,000‑€1,500).; T2: Small businesses will show higher WTP for value-priced units (e.g., €1,000‑€1,500) than homeowners will show higher WTP for premium-priced units.. Decision rule: If homeowners’ average WTP for premium units exceeds small businesses’ average WTP for value units by at least €500, proceed to develop a differentiated premium consumer proposition. If small businesses’ average WTP for value units exceeds homeowners’ average WTP for premium units by at least €500, develop a value‑focused small‑business proposition. If both thresholds are met, pursue both propositions; otherwise, no expansion.. Cost: 18000 euros, 8 weeks.

Favours T1: Do not yet commit to a full consumer proposition. Public evidence shows residential demand for commercial-quality home machines (Alliance Laundry Holdings) and a self-service format capability (Electrolux), but no direct proof of premium pricing or status motivation. Run the proposed premium‑vs‑value messaging pilot to test willingness to pay before investing. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

T1 kept: Simulated evidence SYN-D concerns a label printer reducing packing errors and does not address consumer motivation, pricing, or small business demand. Therefore it neither supports nor contradicts T1. New claim: none. Evidence: SYN-D.

Recommendation: Do not yet commit to a full consumer proposition. Public evidence shows residential demand for commercial-quality home machines (Alliance Laundry Holdings) and a self-service format capability (Electrolux), but no direct proof of premium pricing or status motivation. Run the proposed premium-vs-value messaging pilot to test willingness to pay before investing. Target customer: Homeowners and renters seeking convenience and modern aesthetics, and small businesses with limited budgets for guest laundry and staff facilities.. Value proposition: A differentiated consumer proposition that combines professional-grade performance with design, smart features, and ease of use, enabling homeowners to run their own laundry and small businesses to provide reliable, low-cost guest laundry.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Execute the 8‑week, €18,000 premium-vs-value messaging pilot with 500 respondents to measure willingness to pay for premium‑priced units versus value‑priced units.. Uncertainty: The size of the premium price premium homeowners will pay and whether small businesses will adopt at lower price points remain uncertain. Evidence of actual purchase intent and market share is lacking.. Would change if: If the pilot shows homeowners’ average willingness to pay for premium units exceeds small businesses’ average willingness to pay for value units by at least €500, we would proceed to develop a differentiated premium consumer proposition.; If small businesses show higher willingness to pay for value units, we would develop a value‑focused small‑business proposition.; If neither threshold is met, we would maintain the current professional‑only focus.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Who benefits: Homeowners and renters who lack time or space for a traditional laundry room.. Why behaviour changes: Convenience and time savings become primary purchase drivers; consumers switch from doing laundry themselves to using a self-service machine when it eliminates the chore.. How value is captured: Electrolux can capture value by selling self-service machines directly to consumers through retail channels, offering subscription or pay-per-use models, and charging premium prices for convenience.. Assumptions: Consumer willingness to pay for convenience outweighs cost concerns.; Retail distribution channels can reach target consumers effectively.; Self-service machines meet reliability and performance expectations.. Predictions: In a test market, consumers will choose a self-service machine over a traditional laundry room when convenience is highlighted.; Willingness to pay for a self-service machine will be higher than for a standard professional model.; Repeat purchase rate for self-service units will be higher than for standard units..

T2: Small businesses and commercial users (e.g., gyms, marinas, campsites) face space constraints and need reliable, compact washing/drying solutions that can be placed in limited areas, creating demand for professional-grade machines sold through retail or wholesale channels. Who benefits: Small businesses with limited space and budget that need reliable laundry solutions.. Why behaviour changes: Space constraints and the need for professional-grade performance make compact, reliable machines more attractive than larger, less portable units.. How value is captured: Electrolux can capture value by selling compact professional models through retail and wholesale channels, offering financing or leasing options, and charging premium prices for space efficiency.. Assumptions: Small businesses prioritize space efficiency and reliability over cost.; Retail and wholesale channels can effectively reach these businesses.; Compact professional models meet performance expectations for small-scale use.. Predictions: In a test market, small businesses will choose compact professional models over larger units when space is a constraint.; Willingness to pay for compact models will be higher than for standard professional models.; Adoption rate for compact models in small businesses will be higher than for standard units..

Test "Self-Service vs Compact Model Preference Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with simulated purchase scenarios.. Sample: 500 respondents: 250 homeowners/renters and 250 small businesses (gyms, marinas, campsites). Recruit via panels to ensure diversity in age, income, and geographic location.. Measure: Willingness to pay (WTP) for a self-service machine (convenience) versus a compact professional model (space efficiency). Also measure intent to purchase and likelihood to recommend.. Predictions: T1: Homeowners will show higher WTP for a self-service machine than for a compact model, and both groups will be willing to pay a premium for convenience.; T2: Small businesses will show higher WTP for a compact model than for a self-service machine, and both groups will be willing to pay a premium for space efficiency.. Decision rule: If the average WTP for the self-service machine among homeowners exceeds the average WTP for the compact model by at least 10 percentage points, conclude T1 is supported. If the average WTP for the compact model among small businesses exceeds the average WTP for the self-service machine by at least 10 percentage points, conclude T2 is supported. sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited home cooks considering the same professional-derived combi-steamer were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed identical equipment, brand, cooking specifications, total installed price, warranty, available delivery dates and eventual plumbing/electrical work. One offer bundled an installation coordinator and a site-readiness checklist; the other required the purchaser to arrange the same qualified installers directly. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. All recruited homes were eligible for the stated installation work. The outcome was a paid refundable reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days among all 400 assigned households per arm. There were 32 reservations for the coordinated-installation offer and 72 for the purchaser-arranged offer. This tests whether coordination friction changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show that the appliance fits ordinary kitchens, eliminates drain or power requirements, earns a margin, or justifies diverting resources from professional customers. It does not establish market size or a need for new RATIONAL hardware. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow coordination mechanism changes.

Participants are recruited from home cooks who have used traditional cooking appliances. They are shown two identical combi-steamers (same features, price, and brand) with different descriptions: one emphasizing convenience and time-saving (e.g., 'Replace multiple appliances with one device, save hours in the kitchen.'), and one emphasizing gourmet performance and professional-quality results (e.g., 'Achieve even cooking and precise temperature control like a professional chef.'). Participants indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1 = very unlikely, 7 = very likely) and maximum price they would pay.. Sample: 300 home cooks (150 per condition) recruited via an online panel to ensure diversity in age, gender, and cooking frequency.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1-7) and maximum price willingness to pay for each condition.. Predictions: T1: Higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay for the convenience-focused condition.; T2: Higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay for the performance-focused condition.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent for the convenience condition is at least 1.5 points higher than for the performance condition, proceed with a differentiated home-cook proposition emphasizing convenience. sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited home cooks considering the same professional-derived combi-steamer were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed identical equipment, brand, cooking specifications, total installed price, warranty, available delivery dates and eventual plumbing/electrical work. One offer bundled an installation coordinator and a site-readiness checklist; the other required the purchaser to arrange the same qualified installers directly. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. All recruited homes were eligible for the stated installation work. The outcome was a paid refundable reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days among all 400 assigned households per arm. There were 32 reservations for the coordinated-installation offer and 72 for the purchaser-arranged offer. This tests whether coordination friction changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show that the appliance fits ordinary kitchens, eliminates drain or power requirements, earns a margin, or justifies diverting resources from professional customers. It does not establish market size or a need for new RATIONAL hardware. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow coordination mechanism changes.

Test "Subscription vs Premium Messaging Pilot" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants are recruited from a panel of home cooks (n=500). Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: Group A receives a description of a subscription-based combi-steamer that automates cooking and delivers recipes, with a monthly fee of €9.99. Group B receives a description of a premium-priced combi-steamer that emphasizes precision cooking and professional-grade results, with a price of €1,299. Both groups are shown a neutral product description to control for brand awareness. Participants are asked to indicate their likelihood to purchase (1-7) and the maximum price they would pay.. Sample: 500 home cooks recruited from an online panel, balanced across age, gender, and cooking frequency.. Measure: Purchase intent measured on a 1-7 scale and maximum price willingness to pay.. Predictions: T1: Group A will show higher purchase intent and willingness to pay than Group B.; T2: Group B will show higher purchase intent and willingness to pay than Group A.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent for Group A is at least 1.5 points higher than Group B (i.e., Group A average >= 4.5 and Group B average <= 3.5), we conclude that the subscription model (T1) is more attractive. If the difference is less than 1.5 points, we conclude that the premium positioning (T2) is more attractive. If the difference is not statistically significant, we recommend further testing.. Cost: 20000 euros, 12 weeks.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited home cooks considering the same professional-derived combi-steamer were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed identical equipment, brand, cooking specifications, total installed price, warranty, available delivery dates and eventual plumbing/electrical work. One offer bundled an installation coordinator and a site-readiness checklist; the other required the purchaser to arrange the same qualified installers directly. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. All recruited homes were eligible for the stated installation work. The outcome was a paid refundable reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days among all 400 assigned households per arm. There were 72 reservations for the coordinated-installation offer and 32 for the purchaser-arranged offer. This tests whether coordination friction changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show that the appliance fits ordinary kitchens, eliminates drain or power requirements, earns a margin, or justifies diverting resources from professional customers. It does not establish market size or a need for new RATIONAL hardware. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow coordination mechanism changes.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited home cooks considering the same professional-derived combi-steamer were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed identical equipment, brand, cooking specifications, total installed price, warranty, available delivery dates and eventual plumbing/electrical work. One offer bundled an installation coordinator and a site-readiness checklist; the other required the purchaser to arrange the same qualified installers directly. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. All recruited homes were eligible for the stated installation work. The outcome was a paid refundable reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days among all 400 assigned households per arm. There were 72 reservations for the coordinated-installation offer and 32 for the purchaser-arranged offer. This tests whether coordination friction changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show that the appliance fits ordinary kitchens, eliminates drain or power requirements, earns a margin, or justifies diverting resources from professional customers. It does not establish market size or a need for new RATIONAL hardware. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow coordination mechanism changes.

Method: Online survey with two parallel arms: Arm A offers a smart, subscription-based combi-steamer at a fixed price; Arm B offers a premium, high-performance combi-steamer at a fixed price. Participants are randomly assigned to one arm. Both arms include a willingness-to-pay (WTP) question and a purchase intent question.. Sample: 500 adult home cooks (aged 25-55) recruited via an online panel, balanced across both arms.. Measure: 1) Percentage of participants who indicate they would purchase the device at the given price. 2) Average WTP (in euros) for each arm. 3) Purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1‑2 "Very unlikely" to 7 "Very likely").. Predictions: T1: Arm A will show at least 30% purchase intent and an average WTP at least 20% of the device price, indicating demand for a subscription-based model. Arm B will show lower purchase intent and lower WTP.; T2: Arm B will show at least 25% purchase intent and an average WTP at least 20% of the device price, indicating demand for a premium, high-performance model. Arm A will show lower purchase intent and lower WTP.. Decision rule: If Arm A’s purchase intent is at least 30% and its average WTP is at least 20% of the device price, proceed with a subscription-based home‑cook proposition. If Arm B’s purchase intent is at least 25% and its average WTP is at least 20% of the device price, proceed with a premium, high‑performance home‑cook proposition. If neither arm meets its threshold, do not expand into either segment.. Cost: 8000 euros, 6 weeks.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 households already using a compatible drinking-water purifier received the same membrane specifications, water-quality information, brand, warranty and total annual price. Half were offered a prepaid plan with scheduled cartridge delivery and replacement reminders; half were offered a prepaid self-service cartridge plan without that delivery schedule or reminders. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid plan enrollment remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned households per arm. This what-if assumes an authorised operator can legally supply and service the offer; it does not change the dossier evidence about Aquaporin's insolvency or financing. There were 120 plan enrollments in the scheduled-delivery-and-reminder plan arm and 60 in the self-service cartridge plan arm. This tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under that conditional supply assumption, not membrane efficacy, correct long-term filter use, market size, company solvency or Aquaporin's ability to fund an offer. An unchanged business recommendation can be justified by those other constraints.

Test "Premium vs Sustainability Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging condition. Participants view a product description of a differentiated home water purifier (e.g., premium taste and purity) and a description emphasizing sustainability and plastic waste reduction. Sample: 300 adult consumers in Denmark, recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and income. Randomly assigned to one of two conditions: Premium Condition (premium taste and purity messaging) or Sustainability Condition (sustainability messaging).. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑2 to 7) for each condition.. Predictions: T1: Premium Condition will yield a mean purchase intent score ≥ 5.5, while Sustainability Condition will yield a mean score ≤ 4.5.; T2: Sustainability Condition will yield a mean purchase intent score ≥ 5.5, while Premium Condition will yield a mean score ≤ 4.5.. Decision rule: If Premium Condition mean ≥ 5.5 and Sustainability Condition mean ≤ 4.5, conclude T1 is supported. If Sustainability Condition mean ≥ 5.5 and Premium Condition mean ≤ 4.5, conclude T2 is supported. If both conditions meet their respective thresholds, both theories are supported. If neither condition meets its threshold, conclude no evidence for either theory.. Cost: 2000 euros, 4 weeks.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 households already using a compatible drinking-water purifier received the same membrane specifications, water-quality information, brand, warranty and total annual price. Half were offered a prepaid plan with scheduled cartridge delivery and replacement reminders; half were offered a prepaid self-service cartridge plan without that delivery schedule or reminders. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid plan enrollment remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned households per arm. This what-if assumes an authorised operator can legally supply and service the offer; it does not change the dossier evidence about Aquaporin's insolvency or financing. There were 120 plan enrollments in the scheduled-delivery-and-reminder plan arm and 60 in the self-service cartridge plan arm. This tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under that conditional supply assumption, not membrane efficacy, correct long-term filter use, market size, company solvency or Aquaporin's ability to fund an offer. An unchanged business recommendation can be justified by those other constraints.

Test "Premium vs Sustainability Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging condition. Participants view a product description of a differentiated home water purifier (e.g., premium taste and purity) and a description emphasizing sustainability and plastic waste reduction. They are then asked to indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1‑2 "Very unlikely" to 7 "Very likely").. Sample: 300 adult consumers in Denmark, recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and income. Randomly assigned to one of two conditions: Premium Condition (premium taste and purity messaging) or Sustainability Condition (sustainability messaging).. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑2) for each condition.. Predictions: T1: Premium Condition will yield a higher average purchase intent score than Sustainability Condition.; T2: Sustainability Condition will yield a higher average purchase intent score than Premium Condition.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent score for Premium Condition is at least 1.5 points higher than for Sustainability Condition, proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition focused on premium taste and purity. If the difference is less than 1.5 points, do not invest in a differentiated proposition and consider other alternatives.. Cost: 15000 euros, 6 weeks.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 households already using a compatible drinking-water purifier received the same membrane specifications, water-quality information, brand, warranty and total annual price. Half were offered a prepaid plan with scheduled cartridge delivery and replacement reminders; half were offered a prepaid self-service cartridge plan without that delivery schedule or reminders. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid plan enrollment remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned households per arm. This what-if assumes an authorised operator can legally supply and service the offer; it does not change the dossier evidence about Aquaporin's insolvency or financing. There were 60 plan enrollments in the scheduled-delivery-and-reminder plan arm and 120 in the self-service cartridge plan arm. This tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under that conditional supply assumption, not membrane efficacy, correct long-term filter use, market size, company solvency or Aquaporin's ability to fund an offer. An unchanged business recommendation can be justified by those other constraints.

T1: Consumers will adopt a differentiated home water purifier if they perceive it as a premium, health‑focused product that offers superior taste and purity, leading them to pay a premium price. Who benefits: Health‑conscious consumers seeking higher purity and better taste in drinking water.. Why behaviour changes: If consumers shift from viewing water purifiers as a necessity to a lifestyle or health product, they will be willing to purchase a premium‑priced purifier that justifies the cost.. How value is captured: Aquaporin can capture value by pricing the differentiated product at a premium, selling through direct‑to‑consumer channels or premium retailers, and leveraging brand positioning as a premium water‑purification solution.. Assumptions: Consumers are willing to pay more for perceived health and taste benefits.; The premium positioning can be effectively communicated to the target segment.; Distribution channels can reach the premium segment without significant cost.. Predictions: In a test offering a premium‑priced differentiated purifier, purchase intent or actual sales will be higher than for a standard‑priced model.; Surveyed consumers will rank taste and purity as top reasons for purchasing the premium product..

T2: Consumers will adopt a differentiated home water purifier if it is marketed as a sustainable, eco‑friendly product that reduces plastic waste, leading them to choose it over conventional purifiers. Who benefits: Environmentally conscious consumers who prioritize reducing single‑use plastic consumption.. Why behaviour changes: If consumers associate water purifiers with sustainability and waste reduction, they will be motivated to switch from existing products, even if the cost is higher.. How value is captured: Aquaporin can capture value by positioning the product as a sustainable solution, pricing it at a premium for eco‑conscious buyers, and selling through channels that emphasize environmental messaging.. Assumptions: Consumers are willing to pay more for a product that reduces plastic waste.; Environmental messaging can effectively influence purchase decisions.; Distribution channels can highlight sustainability attributes without compromising margins.. Predictions: In a test offering a sustainability‑focused differentiated purifier, purchase intent or actual sales will be higher than for a standard‑priced model.; Surveyed consumers will rank sustainability as a top reason for purchasing the product..

Test "Smart vs Premium Combi-Steamer Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with simulated purchase intent and willingness-to-pay (WTP) questions. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: Smart Group (smart, subscription-based combi-steamer) or Premium Group (premium, high-performance combi-steamer). Both groups see the same product description and price points.. Sample: 500 adult home cooks (aged 25-55) recruited via an online panel, balanced across both groups.. Measure: Purchase intent (binary: "Would buy?"), WTP (percentage of price paid), and stated reason for purchase (open-ended).. Predictions: T1: Smart Group will show higher purchase intent and WTP than Premium Group, indicating demand for convenience and recurring revenue.; T2: Premium Group will show higher purchase intent and WTP than Smart Group, indicating demand for professional-grade cooking performance.. Decision rule: If Smart Group purchase intent >= 40% and WTP >= 30% of price, conclude T1 is supported. If Premium Group purchase intent >= 40% and WTP >= 30% of price, conclude T2 is supported. If neither condition is met, conclude neither theory is strongly supported. If both conditions are met, conclude both theories are supported and further differentiation is needed.. Cost: 20000 euros, 12 weeks.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 household washing-machine buyers eligible for the same professional-derived washer offer were assigned equally to two descriptions. Both descriptions showed the same machine, brand, price, warranty, availability, service terms and verified specifications. One emphasized durability and repairability; the other emphasized washing performance and the upfront price. No discount or extra service was added. The outcome was a paid, refundable purchase reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned buyers per arm. There were 32 reservations in the durability-and-repairability description arm and 72 in the performance-and-price description arm. This tests the incremental effect of the description in this recruited population, not actual appliance lifetime, delivery capability, market size, profitability or sustained repurchase. A weaker result would not refute a different channel or product theory.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 home espresso enthusiasts considering the same Simonelli single-group machine were assigned equally to two offers. Machine, brand, price, warranty, availability and total contact time were identical. One offer included a structured hands-on home-barista setup lesson; the other included an equal-length product-specification orientation without a skill lesson. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid, refundable machine reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned enthusiasts per arm. There were 72 reservations in the home-barista-lesson offer arm and 32 in the product-specification-orientation offer arm. This tests the incremental effect of this learning offer among recruited enthusiasts, not a need for a new machine, demand among ordinary coffee drinkers, commercial margins or lasting skill retention. It does not show that every hobby or status mechanism is true or false.

Participants are recruited from home barista communities and asked to rank importance of professional taste, control, convenience, and price when choosing espresso equipment. Test "Willingness-to-Pay Survey for Home Espresso Machines" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with a choice-based conjoint design. Participants are randomly assigned to either a lifestyle segment (focusing on personal coffee experience and premium price) or a remote work segment (focusing on home office convenience and compact design). Each participant views a product description of a Simonelli home machine and is asked to indicate their maximum price they would pay and likelihood to purchase.. Sample: 500 respondents: 250 from lifestyle segment and 250 from remote work segment, recruited via online panels to ensure geographic diversity.. Measure: Average maximum price willingness to pay (EUR) and purchase intent (1‑10 scale) for each segment.. Predictions: T1: Lifestyle segment will show higher average maximum price and purchase intent than remote work segment.; T2: Remote work segment will show higher average maximum price and purchase intent than lifestyle segment.. Decision rule: If the average maximum price in the lifestyle segment is at least 20% higher than in the remote work segment, and the purchase intent difference is at least 15 points in favor of lifestyle, then T1 is supported and a differentiated lifestyle proposition is recommended. If the remote work segment's average price is at least 20% higher than the lifestyle segment, and the purchase intent difference is at least 15 points in favor of remote work, then T2 is supported and a remote work‑focused proposition is recommended. If neither segment’s price is significantly higher than the other, and the purchase intent difference is less than 15 points, the evidence is inconclusive and no expansion is recommended.. Cost: 15000 euros, 6 weeks.

Test "Self-Service vs Compact Machine Purchase Intent Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with simulated purchase scenarios. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: Group A sees a self-service laundry unit described as a consumer‑operated solution for multi‑family buildings and gyms, emphasizing convenience and time savings.
